title: Link aggregation (LACP) and Power over Ethernet (PoE)

videos.script: In the last lesson, a second cable between two switches was either a loop or a spare that sat blocked. {{blocked}} This lesson gives both cables a job. Link aggregation tells the two switches that their cables are one logical port. Spanning tree sees one link, so nothing is blocked, and traffic spreads across both. {{bundle}} You will build that bundle with LACP, the protocol the two ends use to agree on it, and read the kernel's report of the negotiation, line by line. {{proc}} Then you will count frames on each cable and see why one conversation always stays on one cable. {{hash}} And you will pull a cable in the middle of a ping. Twenty pings go out, and twenty come back. {{pull}} The second half is power. Power over Ethernet runs phones, access points and cameras from the switch, down the same cable. {{poe}} The lab cannot do this one: a virtual cable carries no electricity. So you will learn the standards and their numbers, and work out a switch's power budget by hand. {{budget}}
